newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zairean rebels assure Belgium on help for refugees.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels assure Belgium on help for refugees.

text.p: Belgium said on Wednesday it had won assurances from Zairean rebels that they would let international humanitarian organisations help refugees caught up in the country's war to return home.

A spokesman for Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said the minister had sent a message to the entourage of rebel alliance leader Laurent Kabila asking for "constructive cooperation" with the humanitarian organisations on the ground.
"The alliance has given its assurance concerning the freedom of action of these organisations in (the alliance occupied) region," spokesman Jan Luykx told a weekly news briefing.

"It agreed to transit centres and 'way stations' - stops on route -- being established by these organisations to help the refugees go home. (However) the alliance is against setting up camps for the refugees," Luykx added.

Since they took up arms last October to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko, rebels have seized a quarter of Africa's third largest country and now have their sights set on Lubumbashi, capital of the mineral-rich Shaba province.

Earlier this week Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) ordered thousands of Burundian and Rwandan refugees to leave Lula camp near Kisangani, in the northeast, and move south away from the town for security reasons.
The Tutsi-dominated rebels fear the refugees include former Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen who had a major role in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
Aid workers say nearly 20,000 sick and exhausted refugees from the Lula camp are now straggling nearly 20 km (12 miles) along a jungle path.

Another 60,000 Hutu refugees are also trapped south of Kisangani after fleeing rebel fighting, while on Monday the U.N. refugee agency said up to 30,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees who fled camps around Goma and Bukavu had arrived at a village in east Zaire's Masisi region saying they wanted to return home.
